tool_input.content:
Cluster: kind-aurora-lab (on-prem, cluster_id kubeconfig-72ec91c49951c05d), namespace shop, deployment "api".

**Pattern:** Deployment api went from revision 1 (single "api" container, healthy) to revision 2, which added a "log-shipper" sidecar container with resources.limits.memory=16Mi, but the sidecar's command does `buf=bytearray(40*1024*1024)` on startup — 2.5x its own memory limit. Container gets OOMKilled (exit 137) within seconds of every start, kubelet enters BackOff, pod stays 1/2 Ready indefinitely, deployment never reaches MinimumAvailable -> triggers KubePodCrashLooping alert. The main "api" container itself was healthy throughout (Restart Count 0) — the crash was entirely from the sidecar.

**Why it matters:** A crash-looping sidecar can keep an otherwise-healthy pod/deployment unavailable. Don't assume the main app container is the problem just because the pod/deployment is reported unhealthy — check ALL containers in `kubectl describe pod`, not just the primary one.

**How to apply / diagnose quickly:**
1. `kubectl get pods -n <ns>` — look at READY column (e.g. "1/2") to spot partial container readiness, not just restart count.
2. `kubectl describe pod <pod>` — check every container's State/Last State/Reason/Exit Code, not just the first.
3. Compare `resources.limits.memory` against what the container's command/code actually needs/allocates.
4. Check `kubectl get replicaset -n <ns> -o wide` to see if a previous (healthy) ReplicaSet still exists as a rollback target before suggesting `kubectl rollout undo`.
5. Fix options: rollback deployment to prior revision (fast mitigation), or raise the sidecar's memory limit to match actual usage / fix the sidecar code to not over-allocate (fix-forward, addresses root cause).
tool_input.description: KubePodCrashLooping on shop/api: root cause was a log-shipper sidecar with 16Mi memory limit but code that allocates a 40MB buffer on startup, guaranteeing OOMKill every restart
tool_input.title: shop/api CrashLoop caused by log-shipper sidecar OOM

thoughts.content: Confirmed. The api deployment is on revision 2 (generation 2) — revision history shows the previous ReplicaSet api-f64486c4c (single container, no log-shipper) was healthy (1/1 Running) and is being scaled down as the new revision rolls out. Let me verify rollback is possible.

Investigation Summary — KubePodCrashLooping / shop/api (CONFIRMED)

Symptom verification: kubectl get pods -n shop confirms the alert is accurate — api-7d4b6f6f7d-d68bn and api-7d4b6f6f7d-sbf8m show 1/2 Ready, RESTARTS: 3 (in ~70s), with the log-shipper container in Terminated/OOMKilled, Exit Code 137 state and kubelet emitting BackOff restarting failed container log-shipper. Deployment status confirms impact: MinimumReplicasUnavailable, unavailableReplicas: 2.

Root cause (confirmed via kubectl describe pod): Deployment api is on generation 2 / revision 2. This revision added a second container, log-shipper, with:
resources.limits.memory: 16Mi
Command: buf=bytearray(4010241024) — i.e., it unconditionally allocates a 40MB buffer on startup, 2.5x its own memory limit.

This guarantees an immediate OOMKill every time the container starts (confirmed: started 16:54:33 → killed 16:54:34; started 16:54:59 → killed 16:54:59; Restart Count 3 within 70s). The api container itself is healthy (Ready: True, Restart Count: 0) — the crash loop is caused entirely by the sidecar, but because both containers share a pod, the pod never reaches Ready, so the deployment can't reach minimum availability and keeps cycling pods.

Ruled out:
Node resource pressure / node issue: all 3 nodes Ready (kubectl get nodes -o wide), and sibling pods (redis, frontend, worker, loadgen) on the same two worker nodes are Running 1/1 with 0 restarts — not a node-wide problem.
api container crash: Restart Count: 0, state Running/Ready: True — the main app process is not the one crashing.
Readiness-probe-only noise: the Unhealthy readiness events are transient (pod just starting, 10-20s window) and not the restart driver — restarts are explicitly OOMKilled on log-shipper, not probe-triggered kills.

Timing explanation: Alert fired right after the new revision (deployment.kubernetes.io/revision: "2", rollout started 16:54:12) was rolled out, replacing the previously healthy single-container ReplicaSet api-f

Saved the root-cause pattern to memory for future reference.
